title: A finite flat algebra is rank one when it is rank one modulo a Zariski-pair ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (the intersection of all maximal ideals of $A$). Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$, as an $A$-module, is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], finitely presented (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus m}\to A^{\oplus n}\to B\to0$ of $A$-modules for some $m,n\ge0$) and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. If the induced map $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism, then $B$ has rank $1$ at every prime of $A$: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the localization $B_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module of rank $1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski), line 2265: finite presentation of B as a module plus flatness makes B finite locally free (Algebra Lemma 00NX); the quotient isomorphism gives rank one on V(I), and local constancy plus I in the Jacobson radical gives rank one everywhere

proof.text: Since $B$ is a finitely presented and flat $A$-module, it is a finite projective $A$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-flat-module-projective] (Stacks 00NX, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2)). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the localization $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finite free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module, say of rank $r(\mathfrak p)$, and the function $r:\operatorname{Spec}A\to\mathbf N$ is locally constant for the Zariski topology.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0ELZ, sentence 'Hence $B$ is a finite locally free $A$-module by Algebra, Lemma 00NX'; rank function of Algebra Lemma 00NX (algebra.tex line 19027)

proof.text: Rank $1$ along $V(I)$. Let $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$ be a prime and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; since $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an $A/I$-algebra. The given isomorphism $A/I\to B/IB$ is $A$-linear, so $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong(B/IB)\otimes_{A/I}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong(A/I)\otimes_{A/I}\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-vector space of dimension $1$. On the other hand $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong B_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{A_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\oplus r(\mathfrak p)}$ because $B_{\mathfrak p}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}^{\oplus r(\mathfrak p)}$ (step 1). Comparing dimensions, $r(\mathfrak p)=1$ for every $\mathfrak p\in V(I)$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0ELZ, 'the module $B$ has rank $1$ along $V(I)$' (written out)

proof.text: Rank $1$ everywhere. Let $U=\{\mathfrak p: r(\mathfrak p)=1\}$; since $r$ is locally constant (step 1), every point of $U$ has an open neighbourhood on which $r\equiv1$, so $U$ is open and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus U$ is closed, $Z=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq A$. If $Z\neq\emptyset$ then $J\neq A$, so $J$ is contained in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ (Zorn), and $\mathfrak m\in V(J)=Z$. But $\mathfrak m$ contains the Jacobson radical, hence $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m\in V(I)\subseteq U$ by step 2, a contradiction. Hence $Z=\emptyset$, i.e. $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is free of rank $1$ over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.
